newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoros islanders demonstrate for secession.
newsitem.headline: Comoros islanders demonstrate for secession.

text.p: Thousands of protesters took part in a rally on Anjouan island on Sunday to press demands for secession from the Comoros republic and a return to French rule.
Witnesses said the islanders applauded 75-year-old Foundi Abdallah Ibrahim, leader of the secessionist movement, when he said: "Our demand is for separation, nothing less."

The meeting, attended by people from all parts of Anjouan, was called after Comoros president Mohamed Taki asked the islanders to submit proposals for ending a constitutional crisis caused by their demand.
The islanders say they have experienced only poverty and political unrest since the main group of the Comoros islands in the Indian Ocean declared independence from France in 1975.
Anjouan's poverty contrasts with the comparative prosperity of the adjoining island of Mayotte, which voted to remain French in 1975.
After Sunday's rally, a procession formed to the office of the Anjouan island governor, where the secessionists raised the French flag and the red flag of the 19th-century Sultan of Anjouan.
France has refused to support the secession call and says the situation on Anjouan is an internal one for the Comoros.

In Paris, a Foreign Ministry spokesman reaffirmed the government's position on Sunday, telling reporters: "We reiterate France's attachment to the territorial integrity of all states including the Islamic federal republic of the Comoro islands.

"We hope that a spirit of dialogue and consultation will prevail in this domestic Comoran affair. We are watching with interest the putting into place of the proposals made yesterday by President Taki," the spokesman said.
